 Judgment

The claimant is before this Court in M.F.A. No. 102920/2018 and the insured of the offending bus bearing reg. no. AP-10/TC-85 in M.F.A. No. 104653/2018, both impugning the judgment and award dated 30.01.2018 passed in M.V.C. No. 368/2014 on the file of the learned Prl. Sr. Civil Judge and CJM and AMACT, Dharwad (hereinafter referred to as the Tribunal) awarding compensation of Rs.4,12,500/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation, to be deposited by respondent no.3/ the insurer.
Parties shall be referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

2. Brief facts of the case is that the claimants being the parents of the deceased Kiran Desai have claimed compensation u/s 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act for the death of their son in the road traffic accident.
It is stated that on the date of accident, i.e., on 31.05.2013, the deceased was driving the bus bearing temporary Reg. No. AP-10/TC-85 and proceeding from Hyderabad to Dharwad.
In the meantime, truck bearing reg. no. AP-07-TA-9828 was coming from the opposite direction.
It is stated that due to the rash and negligent driving of the truck there was a road traffic accident in which the deceased died.

Therefore the claimants being the parents of deceased claimed compensation for the death of their son against respondent Nos.1 to 4, i.e., respondent Nos.1 and 2 being the insured and the insurer of the truck and the respondent Nos.3 and 4 being the insured and insurer of the bus in question.
The respondents have filed their objections denying the contentions of the claimants.
The insured contended that since the vehicle in question was insured with the insurer, it is only the insurance company which is liable to pay compensation.

The insurer of the bus took a contention that deceased was not having valid driving licence to drive the same and therefore there is violation of the terms and conditions of the policy and as such the Company is to be exonerated.
The insurer of the truck in question contended that the bus driver was not holding valid driving licence.

There has been absolutely no negligence on the part of the driver of the truck, no charge sheet was filed against the driver of the truck and the Tribunal held that it is only respondent No.2 who is liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, they prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.

sentences.text: 3. On the basis of the pleadings, the following issues were came to be framed.
1. Whether the petitioners prove that Kiran s/o Shankrappa Desai who died in an accident arising out of driver of Goods Carriage-HMV bearing its Registration No. AP-17/TA-9828 as alleged?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What award or order?
The claimants examined PW1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.12 in support of their contentions.
The respondents got examined RWs.1 to 3 and got marked Exs.R.1 to R.9 in support of their contention.

The trial Court after considering the materials on record came to the conclusion that the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.4,12,500/- with interest at 6% p.a. from respondent No.3, while exonerating respondents No.1, 2 and 4 from their liability.
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimants have preferred M.F.A. No. 102920/2018 and the insured of the offending bus preferred M.F.A. No. 104653/2018.

4. Heard Sri Gopal B. Patil, learned counsel for the owner of the offending bus, Sri J.S. Shetty,
learned counsel for the claimant, Sri Suresh S. Gundi and Smt. Preeti Shashank, learned counsel for insurer of the offending bus and the truck respectively.
5.
Learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the Tribunal committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased.

It has taken the income of the deceased only at Rs.3,000/- per month,
which is on the lower side.
Therefore, he would pray for enhancing the compensation.
Learned counsel further submitted that the driver of the bus was having learner's licence and therefore the insurer cannot be exonerated from paying the compensation.
Hence, he prays for allowing the appeal.
6. Learned counsel for the owner of the bus contended that the driver of the bus was having driving licence to drive the same and therefore the insurer is liable to pay compensation.

7. Learned counsel for the insurers of both the vehicles contended that the defendant was not having valid driving licence and therefore the trial Court rightly exonerated the Insurance Company from paying compensation.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeals.

8. Perused the materials on record including the trial Court records.
9.

The point that arises for consideration in this appeal is:
Whether the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal calls for interference?

10. My answer to the above point as regards M.F.A. No. 102920/2018 is partly in the affirmative and as regards M.F.A No. 104653/2018 is in the negative for the following:

5 REASONS 11. Ex.P.11 is the Learner's Licence relating to the deceased who was driving the bus in question,
issued in his favour for the period from 22.02.2013 to 21.08.2013.

Even though as on the date of accident the learner's licence was valid, it is not the contention of either the claimant or the owner that a person having the regular driving licence had accompanied the deceased.
Therefore, for all practical purposes, the driver was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the offending bus individually.

12. Ex.R.9 is the driving licence particulars issued by the Regional Transport Authority, Dharwad,
pertaining to the deceased Kiran Desai, according to which he was having driving licence to drive LMV (NT) car - motorcycle with gear (NT) for the period from 18.08.2009 to 17.08.2029.

Therefore,
it is clear that the deceased was having the licence to drive the LMV (NT) car and the motorcycle.
But he was not having driving licence to drive the bus in question.
13. ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd., being the insurer has rightly contended that there is violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.

sentences.text: Therefore, it is not liable to pay compensation.
I do not find any reason to reject the same.

The materials that are placed before the Court discloses that the charge sheet was filed against the deceased but no complaint was lodged against the driver of the truck nor any charge sheet is filed against him.

When it already held on the basis of the materials on record, that the deceased was driving the bus in question without having driving licence, in a rash and negligent manner, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that it is only the respondent No.3 being the owner of the bus is liable to pay the compensation, I do not find any reason to interfere with the finding of the Tribunal.
The material on record discloses that deceased was the driver of the offending bus.
As per postmortem report he was aged 23 years.
The claimants have claimed compensation contending that the deceased was earning approximately Rs.3,200/- per month.
In the absence of any material to prove the exact income of the deceased, the same could be taken into consideration.
The annual income of the deceased to be taken at Rs.38,400/-, out of which 1/3rd to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
Therefore, the annual income of the deceased would be Rs.25,600/-.
The appropriate multiplier is 18.
Thus the total compensation towards loss of dependency would be Rs.4,60,800/- (Rs.3,200/- x 12 x 18 x 1/3).
15. The Tribunal has awarded compensation towards funeral and loss of estate as per the second schedule.
Hence, claimant is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.4,65,300/-.
The Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.4,12,500/-
Therefore, they are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.52,800/-.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the appeal preferred by the insured is liable to be rejected while the appeal preferred by the claimant is to be allowed in part.
